text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed higher in quiet dealings. August added $1.0 to close at $320.0 per tonne, while October added $1.3 to close at $316.5 per tonne. There was no fresh news to influence prices.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed higher as the funds became buyers after pressuring the market to five week lows in early trade. Front month October settled 13 points higher at 11.18 cents/lb. March added 9 points to close at 11.30 cents/lb. The floated Thai baht is not likely to affect sugar markets since much of the trade is conducted in US dollars and Thailand has already exported most of its 1996/97 crop. Thailand floated the baht on July 1 after 13 years of fixing it against a basket of currencies dominated by the dollar. In China it was rumored that the government would license the import of as much as 100,000 tonnes of raw sugar for tolling purposes. However, this could not be confirmed and traders remained skeptical. FUNDAMENTALS

DENMARK ** - The weather in the week ended June 29 continued to be changeable with normal temperatures. Precipitation levels since April 1 ranged between 129-183 mm compared to the long term mean of 129-137 mm. Growth is reported to be very good with no diseases detected in the fields. In some regions plants are attacked by aphids. Production prospects are considered to be normal.

NEW ZEALAND ** - Sugar imports in May 1997 amounted to 39,990 tonnes, raw value, up from 6,062 tonnes in May 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first five months of 1997 (January/May) up to 89,296 tonnes against 76,748 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1996 reached 263,774 tonnes against 210,379 tonnes in 1995. The major country of origin in January/May 1997 was Australia with 57,864 tonnes raws against 56,012 tonnes and 28,653 tonnes whites against 18,966 tonnes.

Sugar exports in January/May 1997 reached 6,987 tonnes against 6,714 tonnes in 1996. Total exports in 1996 were 21,407 tonnes compared to 20,270 tonnes in 1995. The major country of destination in 1997 was New Caledonia with 1,916 tonnes whites against 1,662 tonnes.

FRANCE ** - Sugar imports in April 1997 reached 18,943 tonnes, down from 48,371 tonnes imported in April 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first seven months of 1996/97 (October/April) up to 199,951 tonnes compared to 306,116 tonnes in 1995/96. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 476,587 tonnes against 364,140 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin 1996/97 were Reunion with 40,501 tonnes raws against 117,415 tonnes, Swaziland with 25,693 tonnes compared to 41,874 tonnes, Belgium-Luxembourg with 30,664 tonnes whites against 23,723 tonnes and Germany with 24,611 tonnes, up from 16,061 tonnes.

Sugar exports in April 1997 reached 208,844 tonnes against 226,474 tonnes in April 1996. This brought cumulative exports in October/April 1996/97 up to 1.714 million tonnes against 1.922 million tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 2.896 million tonnes against 3.067 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Iran with 179,173 tonnes whites against 158,800 tonnes, Algeria with 147,929 tonnes, up from 42,532 tonnes, Belgium-Luxembourg with 391,902 tonnes against 437,989 tonnes and Spain with 98,250 tonnes, down from 111,424 tonnes.
